newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Motor unit to stall Dorbyl yr shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Motor unit to stall Dorbyl yr shr.

text.p: South African engineering company Dorbyl Ltd is expected to post flat year results depressed by a below average performance from its automotive products business, analysts said on Thursday.

Analysts pooled by Reuters forecast earnings for the year ended September 30 edging up to between 234.2 and 246.0 with consensus at 240.7 cents -- a three percent improvement from last year's 233.6 cents last year.
They expected a dividend of 35.5 cents compared with 30 cents before.
"Dorbyl's motor business tended to be weak. No sparks will be seen from that end," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"I will be surprised if the group posts earnings up more than five percent."

However, analysts said it was difficult to accurately predict earnings growth for the year following Dorbyl's acquisition of a stake in engineering companies FirstPro and Cabris, and an operations swap with LTA Ltd.
A change in management also made forecasting problematic as their management style was unknown.
A recent company restructure was, however, seen providing impetus for limited growth over the past year.
John Arron, analyst at Simpson McKie James Capel, said Dorbyl had been refocussing itself over the last 18 months.
"They have been undergoing a complete reorganisation of the company. They have disposed of non-growth areas with lots of risks," Arron told Reuters.
Dorbyl has moved out of the business of contracting into manufacturing production. The shipbuilding division was also largely scaled down.
Although pleased with Dorbyl's recovery out of loss-making territory 18 months ago, analysts remained concerned about future growth.
"The market has discounted the strong recovery in the company. Investors are saying now that you have done the recovery, how will growth be sustained," an analyst said.
